correctness.rationale: For a hypothetical positive nonfixed two-cycle D(n)=m, D(m)=n, the original primary source proves n,m squarefree with disjoint prime supports. The log derivatives A=D(n)/n and B=D(m)/m are their distinct-prime reciprocal sums and AB=(m/n)(n/m)=1. Hence A+B>=2. Any total of at most 58 distinct primes has sum of reciprocals <=H_58=sum_{i<=58}1/p_i<2. Independent Fraction arithmetic regenerated p_58=271, p_59=277, H_58=1.998740043147044..., and the packaged giant rational numerator exactly. Therefore omega(n)+omega(m)>=59, and one has at least 30 primes. Boundary: this is a necessary bound only, not existence/impossibility of all cycles, and no finite search is used as an infinite proof.
